clue.text: Independent, but irate judge?

parts.note: someone irate is angry, or cross
a bencher sits on the bench, as a judge does; the question mark flags the loose example

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be politically neutral, yet comes across as an angry magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: A CROSSBENCHER sits on the cross benches of the House of Lords, belonging to no party.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbench peer belongs to no political party, so is an independent member.

clue.text: Accountants take in companion to posh dance

indicators.note: the two accountant abbreviations open up to take the other letters inside

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant, so two of them give CA twice
CH is Companion of Honour
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Accountants bring along a friend to a smart ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' has the two accountants close round the companion and posh letters; 'to' only joins those two.
explanation.definitionFit: The cachucha is a lively Spanish solo dance, spelt CACHUCA here.

clue.text: See 'ere, said some sixth-former

indicators.note: some means only part of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A senior pupil, speaking in a broad accent, tells someone to look here.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by sound: 'See 'ere, said' is spoken 'sea ear', a name for the ormer, a shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an abalone, a shellfish also called the sea-ear from its ear-like shell.

clue.text: As a resort, is Tampico pleasant?

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it tells the solver to sort the letters again

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the Mexican port Tampico is a nice place for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' means a holiday town on the surface, but re-sort is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico means congenial and likeable, from Italian and Spanish.

clue.text: Just getting this brings retribution

explanation.surface: Someone notes that merely obtaining something leads to punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Even can mean fair, as in an even deal; and getting even is taking revenge.

clue.text: Thisbe is not in short, a saint

indicators.note: the cut-down name goes inside the word for short

parts.note: curt means short, abrupt

indicators.note: not says the following word is left out of the name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says Thisbe is not, in short, a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not' removes IS from THISBE, leaving THBE, which goes 'in' CURT.
explanation.definitionFit: St Cuthbert was a seventh-century Northumbrian monk and bishop of Lindisfarne.

clue.text: Film actor's run

explanation.surface: A movie star has a spell in the cinemas.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra plays a minor non-speaking part in a film; in cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat.

clue.text: Lay odds on a stand-in horse-or dog

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds offered at a race
a ringer is a horse illegally substituted for another in a race

explanation.surface: A bettor backs a substitute racehorse, or perhaps a greyhound.
explanation.walkthrough: A ringer is a lookalike entered in place of another runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is a spaniel, a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: He often had a hidey-hole — as his retreat perhaps

definitions.text: He often had a hidey-hole — as his retreat perhaps

parts.words: He often had a hidey-hole — as his retreat perhaps
parts.note: describes a clergyman of Elizabethan England, hunted for his faith, who hid in a secret chamber in a country house

explanation.walkthrough: Catholic houses built secret holes, named after the clergy who hid in them, during the persecutions.
explanation.definitionFit: Under Elizabeth I, Catholic clergy hid from searchers in concealed chambers built in recusant houses.

clue.text: French village whence came many a man

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, read as many
Bert is a man's name

explanation.surface: A French village is described as the birthplace of a great many men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whence' only joins the definition to the wordplay; M for 'many' is the Roman thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is the Normandy village that gave its name to the soft cheese.

clue.text: Valve return about to spill

parts.note: a tap is a valve controlling flow

indicators.note: return means the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A plumber's valve comes back round and is about to leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the Latin word for about round to make ER. 'spill' looks like a verb about leaking; it is the noun, a sliver of wood or paper for lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A spill and a taper are both thin strips lit to carry a flame to a fire or candle.

clue.text: Expert in Egypt and Syria once caused a commotion

indicators.note: the word for expert sits in the middle of the old state's initials

parts.note: the United Arab Republic, UAR, joined Egypt and Syria from 1958 to 1961
a pro is an expert, a professional

explanation.surface: A specialist working in the old Arab union stirred up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused a' links: an expert in the old union amounts to a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud public commotion or disturbance.

clue.text: Case of a wild live bat

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters running loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes a specimen box holding a live, untamed bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges LIVE BAT into BLATIVE after A; 'Case' is the grammatical one, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablative is a grammatical case in Latin, used for 'by, with or from'.

clue.text: A pusher is 26's colleague

parts.note: a ram pushes, as a battering ram does

explanation.surface: Someone who shoves is introduced as a workmate of another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is ATHOS; with Porthos, ARAMIS is his fellow musketeer in Dumas.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramis and Athos are two of Dumas's Three Musketeers, comrades in arms.

clue.text: Satisfactory though nothing's left

explanation.surface: Something is acceptable, though all of it has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: All right means acceptable; read as two words it says every part is on the right, none on the left.

clue.text: A Catholic answer to the clue — it's brilliant

parts.note: RC is short for Roman Catholic
in crosswords a light is an entry in the grid, the answer to a clue

explanation.surface: A Catholic gives a reply to the puzzle and is pleased with its cleverness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brilliant' looks like praise for the answer; it describes the lamp's glare.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc light gives an intensely bright glare from an electric spark between electrodes.

clue.text: Free thinker gets unruly tribe into a row

indicators.note: the shuffled word is put into the word for row

parts.note: a line is a row

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A dissenter leads a rebellious tribe into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' turns TRIBE into BERTI, which goes 'into' LINE. 'row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine was once a freethinker in religion, before the word came to mean a rake.

clue.text: Kind of pronoun or connection

explanation.surface: A grammar question asks about a type of pronoun or a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Who, which and that are relative pronouns; a relative is also a family connection, a kinsman.

clue.text: The march past is a doddle

parts.note: to march is to walk in step
over means past, finished

explanation.surface: A military parade is said to be easy work.
explanation.walkthrough: A doddle is British slang for something very easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkover is an easy win, so it is something effortless.

clue.text: 28 accompanying gangster

parts.note: with means accompanying
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A cross-reference is linked to a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is NEVERTHELESS; withal is an old word for that.
explanation.definitionFit: Withal is an archaic adverb meaning nonetheless or in spite of that.

clue.text: King gives decoration to a man

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A monarch awards an honour to one of his subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' and 'to' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is the fairy king in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Rug-ends damaged by pokers

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters are knocked out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: The edges of a hearth rug are scorched by fire irons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pokers' looks like fire irons; it means people who poke.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudgers prod people with an elbow, and so are pokers in the sense of those who poke.

clue.text: Sailor holds the outside of the wheel if in a vessel

indicators.note: the sailor word grips another inside it

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
the rim is the outer edge of a wheel
an is an archaic word for if

explanation.surface: A seaman grips the edge of the ship's wheel when aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: AN for 'if' is old usage ('an it please you').
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a sailing boat with three hulls.

clue.text: Man, for example, positioned under a gangway

indicators.note: in a down clue, this puts the island word below the A

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man is placed beneath a gangway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person; it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passageway between rows of seats, as a gangway is.

clue.text: The stand is crooked? Prod it

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are bent into another order

explanation.surface: Someone sees a stand that leans, and tells another to push it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand for a camera or similar.

clue.text: Murphy not one to talk too much

indicators.note: not says the letter for one is left out

parts.note: murphy and pratie are both informal words for a potato
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone called Murphy is not a person who chatters.
explanation.walkthrough: A murphy is an Irish slang potato; PRATIE, another, loses I.
explanation.definitionFit: To prate is to chatter on foolishly at length.

clue.text: If one of the Lawrences is in the way, let it stand here

indicators.note: the initials go inside the abbreviation for way

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
T.E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Someone says that if a Lawrence blocks the path, leave him there.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is the proofreader's mark meaning keep the deleted text.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is Latin for 'let it stand', used to cancel a correction on a proof.

clue.text: Mount for a French gunman

explanation.surface: A horse is chosen for a French rifleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Athos is the Greek holy mountain; Athos is also one of Dumas's French musketeers, soldiers armed with muskets.

clue.text: "— Eccentric, intervolved" (Paradise Lost)

parts.note: the solver supplies the word that comes just before these two in Milton's line about the mazy dance of the stars

explanation.walkthrough: Milton's line runs 'Mazes intricate, Eccentric, intervolv'd'; the missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word Milton set beside eccentric and intervolved means complicated and tangled.

clue.text: Strange. — three sevens left, all the same

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone finds it odd to have three sevens remaining, but carries on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges THREE SEVENS with L.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevertheless and 'all the same' both mean however, in spite of that.
